reason: The failure it guards against cannot happen with the current code. In register() (tools/overlap_reg.py, worktree e79-6 at a012e32, which contains bc325aa), candidate offsets are tried in order of votes, and the loop breaks at the first one that passes the exact-equality check. Frozen frames cannot outvote the true dt. A duplicated frame produces the bucket {A@t, A@t+1, B@s, B@s+1}, which votes dt0 twice and dt0+-1 once each. Stretches longer than 5 frames make buckets of more than 10 entries, and those are skipped. So the true dt is always tried first. At the true dt, crops of the same source are exact copies: in G-A all 49 accepted pairs had min equal_frac = 1.0, and rejected_voxels = 0. A wrong dt is only ever tried after the true dt has failed the voxel check, which has never happened. Then all 3 of its check frames would also have to land on frozen duplicates. I measured consecutive-frame equality locally: 44b6_0113de3b max 0.022 (0 frames at or above 0.999); in 6bba_05b6850b and 6bba_05db0fb1, 10/99 frames are exact duplicates, all isolated singletons, while the other neighbours are 1-5% equal. That puts the chance of all 3 check frames being duplicates at about 0.1^3. The check therefore adds ~0 on private. It is not harmless either: at the true dt, a +-1 neighbour passes whenever all 3 check frames are duplicates, so the true pair is dropped (~1e-3 per pair, and only on a frozen-frame embryo). The cost is also understated: it needs 6 extra B reads per pair, not 4. Above all, it reopens overlap_reg.py after G-A, which means a G-A rerun, new tests, and rebuilding and re-dummying the user-approved probe and K6 before R8 (27 Sep 12:00Z), all for no measurable value. It is not a closed line in disguise, just an unneeded guard.
fix: Do not add the dt+-1 reads. For a guard at zero read cost, use the evidence register() already has: reject a pair when its accepted offset is not its top-voted candidate, that is, when a higher-voted candidate was rejected for 'voxels'. That is the only way a wrong dt can get through. On G-A the rule changes nothing (rejected_voxels = 0; 49/49 unchanged). Add it only if the probe and K6 are rebuilt for another reason anyway. Otherwise record it as a FACT in CONTEXT: 'dt ambiguity excluded by vote order + break; G-A top-candidate acceptance 49/49; frozen frames are isolated singletons, ~10% in 6bba, 0 in 44b6'. Optionally, log the second-best candidate's votes and offset per accepted pair in the kernel stats (diagnostic only, no decision). If the check is built anyway, pick check frames where B(s) != B(s-1), so no true pair is ever dropped, rather than rejecting on a dt+-1 pass.
realistic_gain: ~0 on public and private (the risk it guards is ~0 given the vote order and exact equality; it would drop about 1e-3 of true pairs, only on a frozen-frame embryo). Real cost: schedule churn on the probe and K6 before R8.
